value.body: A three-year MD in Radiodiagnosis after MBBS. Radiologists interpret X-ray, ultrasound, CT, MRI and mammography, and increasingly perform image-guided procedures. Training is a paid residency in a medical college or teaching hospital, regulated by the National Medical Commission (NMC).

items.label: Course length
items.note: Residency with a thesis; a DNB in Radiodiagnosis is a parallel route

items.label: Ultrasound regulation
items.note: Ultrasound facilities and users must register under it

items.label: Radiation safety
items.note: Atomic Energy Regulatory Board licenses X-ray and CT equipment

items.label: MD Radiodiagnosis seats (India)
items.note: Karnataka (~470) and Maharashtra (~400) list the most seats; the matrix leaves out seats with pending intake-increase applications
items.source: NMC PG seat matrix 2026-27, as reported

value.title: How you get in
value.body: An MBBS with completed internship and medical registration, then a NEET-PG rank. Seats are allotted through MCC counselling (all-India quota, central and deemed universities) and state counselling for state quota seats.

value.title: At a glance
items: Radiodiagnosis seats are usually taken at high NEET-PG ranks in counselling.
Work is largely indoors and screen-based, with fewer emergencies at the bedside than many clinical specialties, but high reporting volumes.
Options after MD include private diagnostic centres, hospitals, teleradiology and teaching; fellowships in interventional, neuro or musculoskeletal imaging are common next steps.
Ultrasound work carries strict PC-PNDT paperwork and legal liability.

value.title: MD Radiodiagnosis seats by state
value.note: Total 3,224 seats. The matrix excludes pending applications for added or new PG seats, so final counts may be higher.
